citation: Karunamurthy A, Vijayan K, Kshirsagar PR, Tan KT. An optimal federated learning-based intrusion detection for IoT environment. Scientific Reports 15:8696, 2025. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-93501-8

A1.evidence: "Before training and testing the dataset is balanced and in the balanced data 70% of the data are used for training and 30% is used for testing" - split method not stated.

A2.evidence: CNN "learns temporal information in the feature sets", Table 2 3x3 kernels; input construction (windows or single records) not described.

A3.evidence: No scaling/normalization/encoding procedure described in Methods or Results.

A4.evidence: Only "After training the learning model for several epochs, the classification model will be sent to server for FL aggregation"; no rounds or epochs in Table 2.

A5.evidence: Table 2 lists baseline hyperparameters; no statement of equal training budget.

A6.evidence: Table 2 gives hyperparameters for NN, RF, NB, DT, GB, MLP and Figs 4-9 show their confusion matrices; no literature numbers quoted.

A7.evidence: "recall, precision, f1-score and accuracy" (Tables 3-10, Figs 11-12); no MCC/balanced accuracy.

A8.evidence: Number of clients and partition of the MQTT dataset across IoT instances not described.

A9.evidence: No repeated runs or dispersion reported.

A10.evidence: Only the MQTT dataset (70/30 split) used.

A11.evidence: Only "Data is provided within the manuscript"; no code link.

notes: Balancing applied before the 70/30 split (quoted in A1), which is itself a leakage risk not covered by A3. Chimp Optimization Algorithm feature selection (17 of 34 features); whether it used test data not stated. Table 2 read from the article PDF (nature.com/...pdf).
